name: Evo Morales
summary: Evo Morales rose to national office through Bolivia’s coca growers’ unions and the Movement Toward Socialism. His presidency expanded public control of strategic industries and social provision and pursued a plurinational constitution recognizing Indigenous self-government. He sought a further presidential term after voters rejected a change to the consecutive-term limit.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The constitutional reforms Morales advanced give Bolivia’s central bank authority to issue currency and execute national monetary policy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Morales signed a family code that regulates civil marriage and its legal effects.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Morales maintained recognized private and communal titles under the agrarian reform law, with constitutional protection conditional on the land’s social function.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: Article 143 of the constitution Morales advanced preserves Bolivian nationality on acquisition of a foreign citizenship and allows naturalized citizens to keep their original nationality.

ban-interest.rationale: Morales signed Law 393, which permits lending at interest while authorizing the executive to cap rates for productive credit and social housing.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Articles 326 and 328 of the constitution Morales advanced have the executive determine monetary and exchange-rate objectives in coordination with the central bank.

civil-marriage.rationale: The Family Code Morales signed provides for civil marriage before an official of the civil registry.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced expressly rejects colonialism and neocolonialism and makes the independence and equality of states principles of its external relations.

conscription.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced imposes an obligation to perform military service as provided by law.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Morales brought the constituent assembly’s draft to referendum and promulgated the resulting constitution, which also requires a constituent assembly for a total overhaul.

constitution-recognises-indigenous-natio.rationale: The constitution Morales championed recognizes Indigenous nations as precolonial peoples and guarantees their self-government within Bolivia.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: In his 2008 climate remarks collected by CLACSO, Morales called for consuming only what people need and ending wasteful luxury.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Morales enacted a law requiring measures to prevent and remedy racism and advanced constitutional guarantees for Indigenous and Afro-Bolivian communities.

death-penalty.rationale: Article 15 of the constitution Morales championed expressly prohibits the death penalty.

direct-action.rationale: Morales repeatedly sought office by election and promulgated a regime retaining elected representatives alongside direct and community participation.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Morales promulgated legislation providing for a direct presidential vote and runoff when the first-round thresholds are not met.

direct-votes.rationale: Morales promulgated an electoral law providing for binding referendums on public policy, laws and constitutional matters.

dominated-front.rationale: Morales signed and later promulgated ratification of Bolivia’s agreement with Cuba and Venezuela for the Bolivarian Alternative and Peoples’ Trade Agreement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 300, which directs the state to build a climate adaptation and mitigation framework across sectors and levels of government.

elective-rulers.rationale: Morales promulgated the electoral regime under which the president is chosen by popular vote.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced imposes enforceable rights and requires a constituent assembly and referendum for reforms affecting those rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Morales advanced constitutional equality guarantees and promulgated legislation outlawing discrimination across grounds including race, sex, religion and disability.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced expressly defines the Bolivian nation as all Bolivians together with its Indigenous nations and peoples, intercultural communities and Afro-Bolivians.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Morales authorized new hydrocarbon exploration in protected areas through Supreme Decree 2366, subject to environmental conditions.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Morales advanced a constitution that makes nonintervention in the internal affairs of other countries and peaceful settlement principles for foreign relations and treaties.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Morales promulgated election rules permitting qualifying foreign residents to vote in municipal elections.

free-public-college.rationale: Articles 17 and 81 of the constitution Morales advanced guarantee free public education at all levels, including higher education.

free-trade.rationale: In his address taking up the G77 chair, Morales rejected free-trade treaties as harmful to countries of both the South and North and urged cooperation agreements instead.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 045, which prohibits discriminatory denial of entry or service in covered public-facing establishments.

future-generations.rationale: Morales signed Mother Earth legislation that requires protecting ecosystems’ ability to regenerate and preserving the conditions needed by future generations.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Morales signed Law 807, which gives eligible transgender adults a process for changing their name, sex marker and image on official records.

gm-crops.rationale: Morales signed Law 300, which restricts genetically modified seeds and directs the state to phase out authorized genetically modified crops. His later decree allowed an accelerated review of two soybean varieties for biodiesel.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Morales’s education reform required intercultural education, with dialogue and exchange of knowledge among Bolivia’s cultural communities.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced places the armed forces under the president and authorizes presidential orders through the defense minister and commander in chief.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: In his 2014 G77 addresses, Morales attributed present warming to greenhouse gas emissions from industrialization and high-consumption economies.

independent-unions.rationale: Article 51 of the constitution Morales advanced requires the state to respect unions’ organizational and ideological independence.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: Articles 190 to 192 of the constitution Morales advanced empower Indigenous authorities to apply their own norms and procedures within their jurisdiction.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Morales advanced constitutional rights to collective title and autonomous territorial management and signed the agrarian reform law providing for collective land claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: In his first inaugural address, Morales said the Indigenous movement sought equal standing with other Bolivians and welcomed workers, professionals, business owners and other groups into shared political leadership.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The constitutional reforms Morales advanced established collective Indigenous rights, and Law 071 recognized the rights of Mother Earth as a collective subject.

land-redistribution.rationale: Morales enacted a reform providing for reversion of land that fails its socioeconomic function, and advanced constitutional provisions for redistribution of public land to communities with too little or none.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Morales enacted Law 913 establishing enforcement, seizure and controls against illicit trade in listed drugs, including cannabis and cocaine, while permitting controlled uses.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Article 71 of the Political Organizations Law Morales signed caps an individual contribution at ten percent of the party’s annual or campaign budget and bans several sources of donations.

local-production.rationale: Morales urged people to give priority to what they produce and consume locally to reduce waste and address unequal access to food.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced rejects wars of aggression, reserves the right of self-defense and makes nonintervention and peaceful dispute settlement principles of foreign relations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Article 244 of the constitution Morales advanced gives the armed forces a duty to uphold the constitution and ensure the stability of the legally constituted government.

minority-language-support.rationale: Morales enacted multilingual education and advanced constitutional official status for Indigenous languages and duties for public administrations to use them.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced provides a process for Indigenous nations sharing ancestral territory to establish territorial self-government.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced replaced the former constitutional religious settlement with state independence from religion and protection for different beliefs.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The plurinational constitution Morales advanced grants Indigenous peoples self-government and authority over their cultural institutions within Bolivia.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced places the constitution above ordinary treaties in the legal hierarchy and treats more favorable human-rights rules as an express exception.

national-resource-control.rationale: Morales ordered the nationalization of oil and gas resources and required producers to transfer output to the state-owned hydrocarbons company.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 071, which recognizes Mother Earth as a collective subject of rights and gives its life systems rights to integrity and regeneration.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Morales used state authority to operate strategic businesses and finance nationwide public health coverage.

no-central-bank.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced establishes the Central Bank of Bolivia and assigns it responsibility for monetary policy and currency issuance.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Morales's Family Code permits divorce or dissolution by agreement or the will of one party without proof of marital misconduct.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The constitution Morales backed explicitly forbids the installation of foreign military bases on Bolivian territory.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Morales’s Education Law explicitly guarantees religious instruction in a secular and pluralist system that also recognizes Indigenous spiritual traditions.

one-party-rule.rationale: Morales promulgated election and party laws giving competing political organizations the legal right to nominate candidates and contest national elections.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: The Family Code Morales signed requires freedom from an existing marriage or recognized union before entering another.

organic-representation.rationale: Morales gave Indigenous communities their own channels of electoral representation while promulgating laws that retained competitive party elections.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Morales described the move from union protest to democratic electoral politics in his inaugural address and set out the goal of community socialism in his later speeches.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Morales enacted laws providing for public input and social oversight in government as well as referendums, popular initiatives and recall votes.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Morales promulgated an education reform that calls for undoing patriarchal social structures and eliminating gender-based differences in roles.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Morales signed Law 300, whose precautionary principle requires action to prevent environmental damage even without scientific certainty.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Morales advanced constitutional protection of Bolivia’s cultural heritage, made Indigenous knowledge part of the education system and signed a law recognizing traditional coca as national heritage.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: After food shortages raised staple prices, Morales decreed that the rural development ministry would set the prices charged by the public food-marketing agency.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Article 19 of the constitution Morales advanced expressly prioritizes low-income and disadvantaged families in social housing, and its economic provisions direct the state to eradicate poverty.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced vests ordinary jurisdiction in public courts and places the armed forces under the president.

property-franchise.rationale: The electoral regime Morales promulgated grants voting rights on the basis of citizenship and age without requiring property ownership.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution Morales advanced makes protection of private property conditional on its social function, and his agrarian reform law enforced a socioeconomic function for agricultural holdings.

proportional-representation.rationale: The constitution Morales championed requires party seat totals in the Chamber of Deputies to reflect proportional vote shares, and his electoral law implements proportional allocation alongside local constituencies.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 341, which guarantees access to public information for participation and social oversight.

public-ownership.rationale: Morales ordered public control of the hydrocarbon industry and transferred the controlling stake in the national telecommunications company ENTEL to the state.

racial-franchise.rationale: The electoral law Morales signed establishes universal suffrage for Bolivian adults across ethnic groups.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 045, which defines racial exclusion as discrimination and penalizes racist acts.

recall-officials.rationale: Morales promulgated an electoral law prescribing procedures for voters to revoke elected mandates before the term ends.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The recall rules Morales advanced allow voters to initiate a recall only after half the term has elapsed and bar a recall vote in the final year.

religious-nation.rationale: Articles 3 and 4 of the constitution Morales advanced define the Bolivian nation by its peoples and communities and establish the state’s independence from religion.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: The electoral law Morales signed sets aside special seats in the Chamber of Deputies for Indigenous constituencies.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 045, which created offenses for disseminating ideas of racial superiority or hatred and for inciting racist violence.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Morales proposed replacing the existing international financial architecture with solidarity funds, stronger regional currencies and financial regulation responsive to developing countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Morales advanced a constitution making the recovery of sovereign Pacific access a permanent objective and pursued that claim with Bolivia’s application against Chile at the International Court of Justice.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Morales presented the transfer of power through the ballot and the refounding of the state as a legitimate democratic and cultural revolution in his first inaugural address.

second-chamber.rationale: Morales retained a two-chamber legislature in the constitutional reform he championed and signed the law governing the election of senators.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 4 of the constitution Morales advanced makes the state independent of religion and protects freedom of belief.

separated-powers.rationale: Article 12 of the constitutional reform Morales advanced establishes separate executive, legislative, judicial and electoral branches and forbids their functions from being consolidated.

simple-living.rationale: In his climate speech collected by CLACSO, Morales called on people to consume what they need and reduce waste and luxury consumption.

single-official-language.rationale: Morales advanced official status for Spanish and Indigenous languages and signed an education law requiring plurilingual education.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Morales convened an elected constituent assembly and advanced the refounding of the state through a new constitution that created a plurinational system with Indigenous jurisdictions and autonomies.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: Morales called for a democratic revolution through the ballot in his first inaugural address and set out community socialism as the goal of his country's political transformation in his later speeches.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Morales vested control of hydrocarbon production and investment in state-owned YPFB and took the controlling stake in ENTEL into state ownership.

state-harmful.rationale: Morales put the state in charge of hydrocarbon production and enacted a state guarantee of free health care.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Morales enacted a framework that makes Vivir Bien the objective of public development policy and incorporated its ethical and community principles into education.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Morales made scientific and technical education complementary to Indigenous knowledge systems and enacted a climate framework combining innovation with ancestral knowledge.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Articles 15 and 114 of the constitution Morales advanced prohibit torture and render statements obtained through it legally void.

unions-good.rationale: Article 51 of the constitution Morales championed recognizes union membership as a means for workers to obtain representation, defense and assistance.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Morales promulgated Law 1152, which brought people outside short-term social insurance into the public health system with free care.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: After the electorate rejected an additional consecutive term in 2016, Morales stood again in 2019 under a court ruling that removed the consecutive limit.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: The electoral law Morales signed sets the voting age at eighteen.

war-builds-character.rationale: In his climate address collected by CLACSO, Morales called for renouncing war and argued that wars bring suffering to peoples while benefiting empires and the companies that profit from them.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Family Code signed by Morales allows either spouse to initiate divorce unilaterally.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Morales enacted agrarian reform provisions on equal land rights and advanced Article 402’s requirement to eliminate discrimination in women’s access to land, tenure and inheritance.

women-suffrage.rationale: Morales promulgated an electoral law expressly protecting equal political rights for women and men.

workers-councils.rationale: Morales enacted an electoral regime in which citizens choose members of a national legislature by universal vote and in special Indigenous constituencies.

workers-own-party.rationale: Morales described the creation of a political instrument by peasant unions and Indigenous organizations so they could contest elections and govern in their own name.
